data.title: Tech Surges After Nvidia Reinstates Huang - Tech Roundup
data.description:
Shares of technology companies surged after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive.

"The question is are his talents so great that it justifies his shortcomings...time will tell," said J.D. Joyce, president of Houston financial advisory Joyce Wealth Management. Joyce said another risk was that Huang's appointment after such "brazen" ethical lapses was that more lapses could occur. "Are they viewing this from a short-term or a long-term basis?" wondered Joyce. "It could be a short-term fix that propels the stock upwards. But if he acts the same way longer term..."

Shares of Anthropic fell, nearing its initial-public offering price, amid concerns about the AI laboratory's profit prospects. Anthropic's bonds look set to be rated in the junk category following its market debut, amid concerns about its plans to raise $900 billion to fund computing power.

Cybersecurity firm Crowdstrike agreed to buy cloud-security firm Zscaler for about $43.9 billion.

data.title: Pryer Aerospace Highlights Workforce Development Needs During Oklahoma's First Space Summit
data.description:
Pryer Aerospace Highlights Workforce Development Needs During Oklahoma's First Space Summit

Pryer Aerospace Highlights Workforce Development Needs During Oklahoma's First Space Summit

PR Newswire

TULSA, Okla., Nov. 23, 2026

At Inaugural Space Summit, Tulsa Manufacturer Highlights Need for Machinists, Assembly Technicians and Quality Inspectors

TULSA, Okla., Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Oklahoma's growing space industry needs additional skilled manufacturing workers to turn aerospace investment into production, Pryer Aerospace President Craig Befort told participants at the inaugural Oklahoma Space Summit on Nov. 18. The Oklahoma Department of Aerospace and Aeronautics and the Oklahoma Space Industry Development Authority hosted the summit to connect spaceflight companies with Oklahoma manufacturers and highlight the state's advanced aerospace opportunities.

Befort shared Pryer's more than 60 years of aerospace manufacturing experience at the summit through the 'Manufacturing Transition' panel. Pryer Aerospace builds complex components and assemblies for customers including Blue Origin, SpaceX, Bell, Spirit Defense, and U.S. defense contractors.

"When people think about the space industry, they picture a launch," said Befort. "Long before that, someone must machine the parts, build the assemblies, and inspect them. Oklahoma manufacturers like Pryer already do that kind of precision work," said Befort.

Pryer's work in aviation and spaceflight gives it a firsthand view of the skills Oklahoma manufacturers already have and the people they'll need as the industry grows.

During the panel, Befort pointed to workforce development as a major challenge for Oklahoma's growing aerospace industry. For Pryer, the need is tied to investments already underway, including expansions totaling 130,000 square feet in the Tulsa area.

"Putting that added capacity to work will take more skilled machinists, assembly technicians, and quality inspectors in Oklahoma," said Befort. Pryer currently has multiple positions open, a situation that other aerospace companies at the summit echoed.

As demand grows across aviation, defense, and spaceflight, summit attendees collectively noted that Oklahoma needs to encourage young Oklahomans to explore careers in aerospace manufacturing and develop the skills to enter the industry.

"We appreciated the opportunity to bring our expertise to the summit to help other companies successfully make the transition to aerospace manufacturing, and the opportunity to share our industry's needs for a stronger talent pipeline," Befort said.  

About Pryer Aerospace
Founded in Oklahoma in 1965, Pryer Aerospace manufactures complex components and structural assemblies for aviation, defense, and spaceflight customers. Its capabilities include precision machining, metal fabrication, and advanced structural assembly. Learn more about Pryer Aerospace at pryeraero.space; learn more about a career at Pryer Aerospace at pryeraero.jobs.

data.title: Monique Johnson Named Chief Financial Officer at AltaSea
data.description:
Monique Johnson Named Chief Financial Officer at AltaSea

Longtime Board Trustee and banking executive brings more than 40 years of financial leadership experience to AltaSea

AltaSea at the Port of Los Angeles, the world’s leading destination for the blue economy, today announced the appointment of Monique Johnson as its new Chief Financial Officer (CFO). Johnson, a longtime member of AltaSea’s Board of Trustees and an accomplished banking executive with more than 40 years of experience, will oversee the nonprofit organization’s financial operations as it continues to modernize its 35-acre campus and advance its mission of developing ocean-based solutions to climate change.

Johnson joins AltaSea’s executive leadership team after over a decade at Beneficial State Bank, a mission-driven financial institution founded by Kat Taylor and Tom Steyer in 2007. Most recently, she served as Senior Vice President and Director of Client and Community Partnerships, following leadership roles in treasury management and retail banking. There, she worked with businesses, nonprofits, and community leaders to strengthen partnerships and support economic opportunity. She has served on AltaSea’s Board of Trustees and as treasurer since 2018, providing financial oversight and strategic guidance during a period of significant growth for the organization.

“Monique has been an invaluable member of our Board for nearly a decade, and we have benefited from the tremendous insight and financial expertise she brings to the table,” said AltaSea President & CEO Terry Tamminen. “Her outstanding work at Beneficial State Bank, a tenant at AltaSea, has allowed us to see firsthand her ability to combine strong financial leadership with a genuine commitment to making a positive impact. We are thrilled to welcome her to our executive team and look forward to the important role she will play in AltaSea’s continued growth.”

Throughout her more than 40-year career in banking, Johnson has held executive leadership positions at several financial institutions, including Wedbush Bank, Imperial Bank, Alliance Bank, and Private Bank of California. She is also a longtime leader in Southern California's nonprofit community, serving on the boards of Junior Achievement of Southern California and the U.S. Green Building Council of California. Johnson is also a member of the Forbes Finance Council and was recognized by the Los Angeles Times as a “Visionary Leader in Finance.” She holds a bachelor's degree in business administration from Iowa State University.

“Having served on AltaSea’s Board for nearly a decade, I have had the opportunity to help this incredible organization grow and see the impact of its work,” said Johnson. “AltaSea is a truly special place. I am proud to be part of this organization and excited to take on this new role to help advance its mission and support its continued growth.”

Now in its 12th year, AltaSea has developed a 35-acre ocean technology campus that is home to innovative climate solutions across a variety of industries, including aquaculture, carbon capture, renewable energy, and ocean exploration. AltaSea also partners with high schools, colleges, and universities to provide educational experiences for the next generation of climate scientists and innovators.

About AltaSea at the Port of Los Angeles

AltaSea at the Port of Los Angeles, located on 35 acres at North America’s leading seaport by both container volume and cargo value, is an ocean technology campus that has become a hub for marine science, research, and education. AltaSea brings together ocean-focused companies, researchers, colleges, and universities to accelerate scientific collaboration, advance the blue economy through business innovation and job creation, and inspire the next generation, all for a more sustainable, just, and equitable world.

For more information on AltaSea, please visit: https://altasea.org.

data.title: Cisco, OpenAI Launch Project to Safeguard Agentic AI
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

Cisco Systems and OpenAI launched an open source project to safeguard agentic artificial intelligence and prevent cyber attacks.

Financial terms of the partnership weren't disclosed. The project, called Shirudo, helps protect running Linux systems without a reboot while teams roll out a patch.

With Shirudo, AI agents can find a vulnerability, build a shield and test that it stops the attack without disrupting the service, the companies said.

"So many teams rely on the same software that it makes sense to build these tools in the open," OpenAI Co-Founder Greg Brockman said. "Now when one team finds a better way to protect a system, others don't have to start from scratch."

data.title: Securities Class Action Filed Against MNTN, Inc. – MNTN Investors Encouraged to Contact Kirby McInerney LLP
data.description:
Securities Class Action Filed Against MNTN, Inc. – MNTN Investors Encouraged to Contact Kirby McInerney LLP

The law firm of Kirby McInerney LLP announces that a class action lawsuit has been filed on behalf of investors who acquired MNTN, Inc. (“MNTN” or the “Company”) (NYSE: MNTN) securities between August 5, 2026 and November 4, 2026, inclusive (“the Class Period”). If you suffered a loss on your MNTN investments, you have until January 19, 2027 to request lead plaintiff appointment.

[CONTACT THE FIRM IF YOU SUFFERED A LOSS]

Investors are encouraged to fill out the contact form above or contact Lauren Molinaro of Kirby McInerney LLP by email at investigations@kmllp.com to discuss your rights or interests in the securities fraud class action lawsuit at no cost.

What Is This Lawsuit About? The lawsuit alleges that MNTN made false and/or misleading statements and failed to disclose that: (i) MNTN materially overstated the Company’s business prospects, considering that MNTN had instituted changes that caused many experienced salespeople to leave MNTN; and (ii) the foregoing materially impacted MNTN’s ability to meet its previously issued guidance for 2026.

On November 4, 2026, MNTN announced its third quarter 2026 financial results, reporting third quarter revenue of $80.3 million, below the Company’s previously stated guidance of $86 million to $89 million, and lowering its full year revenue guidance to a range of $311 million to $314 million, down from $347 million to $357 million. The Company also revealed that its Board of Directors had terminated the employment of MNTN CEO Mark Douglas and COO Christopher Innes, effective December 3, 2026 and December 1, 2026, respectively. Newly appointed CEO Tony Weisman explained the Company’s third quarter financial results, stating, “The company recently made significant changes in the sales team that did not work out, most notably a new compensation structure… They were implemented too quickly, resulting in sales force attrition. We lost about 40% of our experienced quota-carrying sellers, reducing our ability to bring in new business.” On this news, the price of MNTN shares declined by $5.67 per share, or approximately 54.67%, from $10.37 per share on November 4, 2026 to close at $4.70 on November 5, 2026.

[LEARN MORE ABOUT THE LAWSUIT]

The Lead Plaintiff Appointment Process. The federal securities laws permit any investor who acquired eligible securities during the class period to seek appointment as lead plaintiff in a class action lawsuit. Courts do not consider lead plaintiff applications submitted after the relevant deadline. If you choose to take no action, you may remain an absent class member. Learn more about the lead plaintiff process and eligibility requirements here. Courts typically appoint the investor(s) with the largest financial loss in the case and the ability to represent the class rather than investors with simply the largest investment portfolio. Courts regularly appoint individual investors, whether acting alone or as a group, as lead plaintiffs. The rights of any investor who bought shares during the class period are generally already protected. However, lead plaintiffs have the power to influence case strategy and have a say in settlement decisions, as well as decisions concerning allocation of settlement funds among class members.

[LEARN MORE ABOUT THE LEAD PLAINTIFF PROCESS]

What Should I Do? If you purchased or otherwise acquired MNTN securities, have information, or would like to learn more about this investigation, please contact Lauren Molinaro of Kirby McInerney LLP by email at investigations@kmllp.com, or fill out the contact form below, to discuss your rights or interests with respect to these matters at no cost.

Kirby McInerney LLP is a New York-based plaintiffs’ law firm concentrating in securities, antitrust, whistleblower, and consumer litigation. The firm’s efforts on behalf of shareholders in securities litigation have resulted in recoveries totaling billions of dollars. Additional information about the firm can be found on Kirby McInerney LLP’s website.

This press release may be considered Attorney Advertising in some jurisdictions under the applicable law and ethical rules.

data.title: U.S. stocks see best day in more than a year, as return of Jensen Huang revives AI enthusiasm
data.description:
By Christine Idzelis

Monday's session saw another 'V-shaped' rebound for stocks

The stock market saw a big rally Monday as investors appeared to celebrate Jensen Huang being reinstated as CEO at AI giant Nvidia.

Jensen Huang's return as CEO of Nvidia powered a massive bounce in the U.S. stock market on Monday by helping to restore faith in the artificial-intelligence trade.

The S&P 500 SPX surged 4.7% Monday, scoring its largest daily percentage gain since April 9, 2025, according to Dow Jones Market Data. That marked a major shift in investor sentiment around AI, as investors appeared to cheer Huang's return in charge of the semiconductor giant at the center of the AI infrastructure buildout.

To be sure, the rebound was pretty broad-based, with stocks that aren't part of the AI theme tallying big gains as well. Nine of the S&P 500's 11 sectors finished higher Monday.

The entire stock market is behaving "a lot more like an individual security, with a lot of volatility and a lot of sensitivity" to the AI buildout, Kevin Khang, senior global economist at asset-management giant Vanguard, told MarketWatch in an interview Monday.

"The last six months is really the microcosm of what we should be expecting for the foreseeable future," at least for the next 12 months, said Khang. "Expect pretty high volatility and expect the source of the volatility to be something about the sustainability, or the future projected rate, of the AI buildout."

The U.S. stock market has been vulnerable to sudden mood changes around the AI trade, as investors keep reassessing the likelihood that the massive investment in AI infrastructure will yield a suitable return. The S&P 500 is top-heavy, with Big Tech stocks like Nvidia (NVDA) dominating the index, creating more opportunity for powerful swings.

The S&P 500's information-technology sector XX:SP500.45 soared 9% on Monday, as Nvidia's shares skyrocketed and chip stocks SOX broadly also surged, FactSet data showed.

Investors on Monday appeared to be "responding massively to Jensen being reinstated," Khang noted. Even before his reinstatement, however, stocks that had recently sold off amid an unwinding of the AI trade had "started to look very attractive" to some investors, he said.

Monday began with U.S. stock-market futures rallying, a rebound that accelerated ahead of the opening bell after news emerged that Huang was being reinstated as CEO, president and board member at Nvidia.

The Nasdaq Composite COMP soared more than 7% at the opening bell, its biggest gap higher at the open on record going back to 1991, Dow Jones Market Data showed.

Pressure on the U.S. stock market intensified after Huang resigned from Nvidia 11 days ago, adding to the headwinds facing the AI trade.

Check out: Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia saved the stock market - for now. Will the rebound last?

But whether the pain is truly over remains to be seen. Wells Fargo Investment Institute's head of global investment strategy, Paul Christopher, cautioned against rushing into the stock market to make big bets in the market.

"We're not backing up the truck here" to buy stocks, Christopher said in a phone interview. "You could easily have another retest of 7,000" for the S&P 500 index, he noted.

At the root of the stock market's volatility is "who's going to win in AI," according to Christopher, and that is a question that will likely take time to answer.

The Cboe Volatility Index VIX finished Monday at 26.62, down nearly 26%.

The S&P 500 closed Monday at about 7,237. That's after ending Friday at 6910.39, following a brutal drop last week that saw it enter a correction along with Dow Jones Jones Industrial Average DJIA. The tech-heavy Nasdaq, which had entered a correction earlier in November, saw an ugly drop Friday that wiped out its 2026 gains - though its bounce Monday put it back into the green for the year.

-Christine Idzelis
